# On Writing Plainly

Good writing is easy to read, but achieving that ease frequently requires the author to
undertake a surprisingly arduous process of revision, reconsideration, and the systematic
elimination of superfluous subordinate clauses that accumulate during the initial drafting.

Consequently, the experienced practitioner approaches the manuscript with considerable
skepticism, interrogating every elaborate construction and every polysyllabic substitution
to determine whether comprehension would be meaningfully enhanced by a plainer alternative.
